c.tagline: Norway's oil capital and gateway to Pulpit Rock, wrapped around a colorful old harbor.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are expensive and metered, with higher night and weekend tariffs; book via the Rogaland Taxi app or phone, or use a rank, as street-hailing is uncommon. Uber does not operate here, but Bolt is available.

emergency.note: 112 reaches police, 113 ambulance, and 110 fire; 112 also works as the general EU-style emergency number.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The compact downtown around the Vagen harbor, the Stavanger Cathedral, Torget market square, and the pedestrian shopping streets; the walkable central base for first-timers, with restaurants, the Norwegian Petroleum Museum, and the ferry quays all on foot.

The UNESCO-recognized old town of some 170 whitewashed 18th- and 19th-century wooden houses on the harbor's west side, with cobbled lanes, galleries, and the Canning Museum; picturesque and quiet, ideal for atmosphere and photos.

The famously colorful 'Fargegata' street and the surrounding blocks packed with cafes, bars, boutiques, and nightlife just uphill from the center; lively and photogenic, a magnet for younger travelers and a night out.

A characterful residential and increasingly hip district east of the center, home to the Pedersgata food street, breweries, and street art; a laid-back local area for those who want to eat and drink where residents do.

A leafy, upscale residential quarter west of downtown around the Mosvatnet lake and city park; calm and green, good for families and travelers wanting quiet strolls within walking or short-bus distance of the center.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buy tickets in the Kolumbus app or with a travel card; a single ticket is valid across bus, local train, and city boats within its zone for a set time, allowing transfers.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30 AM to around midnight; the Jaeren commuter trains and local passenger boats keep similar daytime and evening hours, with reduced weekend service.
transit.note: Kolumbus runs the region's public transport: an extensive bus network, the Jaerbanen commuter trains south to Sandnes and Egersund, and passenger boats around the fjord and to nearby islands. The center itself is small enough to walk.

car.idp: Not required for EU/EEA and US licenses

Kolumbus bus to Stavanger center (~40 min)

tip.r: Service is included in prices; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service at restaurants is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Skrei and fresh North Sea cod
food.desc: Winter migrating skrei poached or pan-fried with its roe and liver, or year-round cod with brown butter, potatoes and carrot - Rogaland's flagship fish.

places.name: Fisketorget
places.note: Fishmonger and restaurant on the harbour; the standard answer to where to eat fish in town.

places.name: Sjohuset Skagen
places.note: Old timber warehouse on the water serving Norwegian seafood classics in a historic room.

places.name: Renaa Matbaren
places.note: The relaxed bistro arm of the Michelin-starred Re-Naa, strong on seasonal fish.

food.name: Fjord shrimp on bread
food.desc: Sweet cold-water reker peeled by hand at the table and piled onto buttered white bread with mayonnaise, lemon and dill - the local summer ritual.

places.name: Fisketorget
places.note: Buy them by the kilo from the counter or eat a shrimp plate looking over the harbour.

places.name: Shrimp boats at Vagen quay
places.note: Boats sell freshly boiled shrimp straight off the deck in season; bring napkins.

places.name: Sjohuset Skagen
places.note: Sit-down version with the full bread, mayonnaise and lemon spread.

food.name: Kjottkaker
food.desc: Large Norwegian meat patties in brown gravy with mashed swede or potato, peas and lingonberry - the everyday comfort dish of a Rogaland kitchen.

places.name: Patrioten
places.note: Bistro built around Norwegian home cooking; the go-to for meatballs and komle.

places.name: Lura Turistheim
places.note: Old roadside inn just out of town where locals go for traditional plates.

places.name: NB Sorensens Dampskibsexpedition
places.note: Historic quayside emigrant warehouse serving Norwegian classics upstairs and down.

food.name: Komle (raspeballer)
food.desc: Heavy grated-potato dumplings boiled with salted lamb or sausage and served with bacon fat, swede mash and syrup - traditionally eaten on Thursdays.

places.name: Lura Turistheim
places.note: Keeps the Thursday komle tradition; go at lunch and expect a full plate.

places.name: Patrioten
places.note: Reliable in-town komle without driving out to the countryside.

places.name: Kronen Gaard
places.note: Rural manor hotel doing simple traditional Rogaland cooking with local produce.

food.name: New Nordic tasting menu
food.desc: Stavanger punches far above its size - multi-course menus of Rogaland lamb, Jaeren vegetables, fjord shellfish and aged seafood, plus Michelin-level sushi.

places.name: Re-Naa
places.note: The city's flagship fine-dining room and Norway's most decorated kitchen outside Oslo.

places.name: Sabi Omakase
places.note: Michelin-starred omakase counter using Norwegian fish, booked well in advance.

places.name: Eg & Kjott
places.note: Meat-focused alternative built on local farms, fruit and vegetables.

food.name: Svele
food.desc: Thick, soft buttermilk pancakes folded around butter and sugar or brown cheese, sold hot from kiosks and famously eaten on the fjord ferries.

places.name: Ferry kiosks on the Ryfylke routes
places.note: The classic setting - buy one at the counter as the boat crosses the fjord.

places.name: Kiosks around Vagen harbour
places.note: Quayside stands do svele and coffee in the afternoon.

places.name: Island ferries to Vassoy and Byoyene
places.note: Short local crossings from the city centre, with the same griddle behind the counter.

food.name: Lervig craft beer
food.desc: Stavanger's internationally known brewery pours pale ales, stouts and sours in town, alongside a deep-rooted local beer-bar culture.

places.name: Lervig taproom
places.note: The brewery's own bar on the east side, with fresh and experimental pours.

places.name: Cardinal Pub
places.note: Legendary Stavanger beer bar with a huge Norwegian and international list.

places.name: Boker og Borst
places.note: Bookshop-bar on the painted street, a locals' favourite for a pint.

food.name: Akevitt
food.desc: Caraway-and-dill potato spirit aged in oak, drunk in small glasses beside heavy traditional food and always with a beer alongside.

places.name: NB Sorensens Dampskibsexpedition
places.note: Historic harbour house where akevitt with kjottkaker is the traditional order.

places.name: Sjohuset Skagen
places.note: Aquavit list to go with the salted and cured seafood plates.

places.name: Patrioten
places.note: Serves it in the Norwegian way, as a chaser to komle or meatballs.

landmarks: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
Norway's most famous hike ends at this sheer granite platform hovering 604 metres above Lysefjord, an unforgettable day trip from Stavanger.
Gamle Stavanger (Old Stavanger)
Northern Europe's best-preserved wooden town, 170-plus whitewashed 18th-century cottages lining cobbled lanes bright with flower boxes above the harbour.
Stavanger Cathedral (Domkirke)
Norway's oldest cathedral in continuous use, an Anglo-Norman stone church founded around 1125 that anchors the city centre beside Breiavatnet lake.
Norwegian Petroleum Museum
A strikingly designed harbourside museum resembling offshore platforms, telling the story of the North Sea oil adventure that transformed Norway.
Sverd i fjell (Swords in Rock)
Three colossal bronze Viking swords planted in a fjordside hill at Hafrsfjord, commemorating the 872 battle that unified Norway.
Øvre Holmegate
Stavanger's 'colour street', a candy-hued lane of cafés, bars and boutiques whose painted facades make it the city's most Instagrammed block.
Lysefjord
A 42-kilometre glacier-carved fjord of thousand-metre granite walls, waterfalls and mountain goats, best experienced on a sightseeing cruise from Stavanger's harbour.
Norwegian Canning Museum
A wonderfully atmospheric former sardine factory in Old Stavanger, still smoking brisling over oak chips to evoke the industry that built the city.
Valbergtårnet (Valberg Tower)
A 19th-century fire-watch tower crowning the old town's highest point, offering sweeping views over Vågen harbour and the city's rooftops.
Kjeragbolten
A legendary boulder wedged in a mountain crevice a thousand metres above Lysefjord, the daring hiker's photo op of a lifetime.

train.note: The Sorlandet line runs from Stavanger east to Kristiansand (~3 hr) and on to Oslo (~8 hr), while the local Jaerbanen commuter trains serve Sandnes and Egersund frequently through the day. No international rail.

bus.note: Kolumbus regional buses and NOR-WAY / Vy express coaches link Stavanger with Sandnes, Haugesund, Kristiansand, and Bergen.

intl.to: Ryfylke islands & the Lysefjord for Preikestolen (Norway)

ferry.note: Kolumbus passenger boats and car ferries connect Stavanger with the Ryfylke islands and the Lysefjord (for Preikestolen), while the Flaggruten express catamaran (Norled) runs north to Haugesund and Bergen.

half.name: Flor og Fjære
half.blurb: Garden island reached by boat, planted with flowers and shrubs that thrive in a sheltered microclimate.

half.name: Utstein Abbey
half.blurb: Norway's best-preserved medieval monastery, built in the 13th century on an island north of the city.

half.name: Jærstrendene
half.blurb: Long stretch of sandy beach coastline south of the city, popular for walking and surfing.

full.name: Haugesund
full.blurb: Coastal town connected by road and ferry, known as a historic site tied to the unification of Norway.
